headers.comment: Asset filenames carry a content hash, so a changed file is a changed URL. They can be cached indefinitely; Firebase's default of one hour re-fetches them for no reason.

The entry point must never be cached: each release deletes the previous hashed assets, so a stale copy points at files that 404. Header rules match the requested URL, not the rewrite target, so a source of /index.html missed / and every route served through the rewrite; this matches any extensionless path.
Regenerated weekly and unhashed, so revalidate rather than serve a stale snapshot.
The app frames nothing and should not be framed.
